fi-sphaeramia-nematoptera.title: Pajama Cardinalfish
fi-sphaeramia-nematoptera.summary: A slow, peaceful cardinalfish with a yellow face, dark band and polka-dot rear. Good for calm reef tanks.
rows: About 3.5 in; wild record 8.5 cm (3.3 in) TL (FishBase)
Can be kept in small groups; they settle a pecking order without much fighting
Indo-Pacific: Java to Fiji, north to the Ryukyu Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef
notes: Give it hiding places in rockwork and calm tankmates.

fi-apogon-maculatus.title: Flame Cardinalfish
fi-apogon-maculatus.summary: A red cardinalfish from the western Atlantic with big eyes, a dark eye stripe and a black spot under the rear dorsal fin. It is nocturnal and spends the day in caves and shaded crevices; dim lighting brings it out more.
rows: About 6 in (Top Shelf adult size); wild record 11.1 cm (4.4 in) TL (FishBase)
Carnivore. Foods: mysis shrimp, chopped marine fish flesh, chopped crustacean flesh, clam, frozen meaty marine preparations, marine flake food, enriched zooplankton
Western Atlantic: Canada to Massachusetts (USA), Bermuda, Bahamas, and Gulf of Mexico to Brazil
notes: Safe with corals, but its large mouth can take small ornamental shrimp and very small fish.
